results.title: Nebius did exactly what it said it would. Last week's Pulse flagged the on-demand increases Nebius had posted for October 1. Our October 4 catalog capture yesterday shows them in place, in … | Bobby Clay
results.author: Bobby Clay
highlights:
Nebius did exactly what it said it would. Last week's Pulse flagged the on-demand increases Nebius had posted for October 1. Our October 4 catalog capture yesterday shows them in place, in dollars per GPU-hour:

H100: $3.85 to $4.50
H200: $4.50 to $5.40
B200: $7.15 to $8.50
B300: $7.85 to $9.50

That changed the lowest observed H100 list price across the nine providers we track. On September 27 it was Nebius at $3.85 per GPU-hour. On October 4 it was Crusoe at $3.90.
Everything else held. Of 14,001 GPU price listings in the October 4 catalog, 13,996 matched a September 27 listing, and the 20 Nebius listings were the only verified changes above 1%.

The transaction side moved on its own path. OCPI for H200 went from $4.84 on September 28 to $5.57 on October 4. Over the same stretch, the lowest H200 list price we track held at $4.29 (Crusoe). List prices and transaction prices measure different things, and this week the gap between them widened. If you buy on-demand capacity from a Neocloud, posted price notices are worth tracking. This one landed on schedule, to the cent.

The full issue, with every provider's lowest observed price and the method notes, is here:
https://lnkd.in/efqfwQWm

These are public catalog list prices, not live quotes, and a listing does not establish capacity or orderability.

results.title: Nebius GPU prices rise across the board, up to… · Slicast
highlights:
Trade press Slicast · October 1, 2026 at 21:01 UTC · Global · Source: KuCoin News

A notable shift is emerging in the AI computing power market: while cloud providers continue to expand their data centers, rental prices for certain high-end GPUs are not declining with increased supply—they continue to rise.

According to a price adjustment notice sent by Nebius to its customers, effective October 1, 2026, the company plans to increase prices for multiple on-demand GPU instances by approximately 17% to 21%. The proposed hourly rates per GPU are: H100 rising from $3.85 to $4.50 (a 16.9% increase), H200 from $4.50 to $5.40 (20% increase), B200 from $7.15 to $8.50 (18.9% increase), and B300 from $7.85 to $9.50 (21% increase).

results.title: Recompute Token Cost Before Q4 GPU Reservations — The Serving Desk
results.author: 3 MIN
highlights:
GPU reservations trade committed capacity for a fixed rate, but a fixed rate can become a stale rate when on-demand prices move. The arithmetic is simple: cost per token equals the GPU-hour rate divided by tokens per GPU-hour, so the percentage change in rate becomes the percentage change in token cost when throughput holds. Nebius, an AI cloud provider, is repricing its Nvidia GPU fleet on October 1, the second on-demand reset in three months.

The H100 moves from $3.85 to $4.50 per GPU-hour, a 16.9% increase. H200 and B200 rates move to $5.40 and $8.50 per GPU-hour, increases of 20% and 18.9%. The B300 jumps from $7.85 to $9.50 on October 1, a 21% increase.

results.title: "AI compute gets cheaper every year" stopped being true on October 1. | Aslam Ahamed
results.author: Aslam Ahamed
highlights:
"AI compute gets cheaper every year" stopped being true on October 1.

That day, Nebius put a new on-demand rate card into effect. Not a promo ending. A higher price for the same hardware.

1. H100 went from $3.85 to $4.50 per GPU-hour. That's +17%, about $468 a month for one GPU running around the clock. An 8-GPU node now costs $3,744 more per month for the same work.

2. The newest chips took the biggest hit. B300 rose 21% ($7.85 to $9.50). H200 +20%. B200 +19%. The scarcer the hardware, the steeper the hike.

October 2 is after the effective date, and the page still shows both numbers. The left-hand label is still “On-demand, GPU-hour.” The right-hand label is “GPU-hour (Effective October 1, 2026).” A customer cannot tell, from the page alone, which figure the console will bill.

GPU Finder’s Nebius page, with availability checked at 06:23 UTC on October 2, still listed one-GPU on-demand rates of $3.85 for the H100, $7.15 for the B200, and $7.85 for the B300. Those are the old column. The same check already showed the H200 at $5.40, the new column, with a spot print of $2.45 beside it. The H100 spot print on that row was $2.15. The tracker has not frozen. It has moved one of the four headline GPUs and left the other three on the pre-October number. Treating the whole book as repriced at midnight on October 1 would be tidier, and it would be wrong.

results.title: Nebius 1 жовтня підвищить ціни на графічні процесори NVIDIA максимум на 21% | Новини Gate | Gate News
results.author: GateNews
highlights:
# Nebius 1 жовтня підвищить ціни на графічні процесори NVIDIA максимум на 21%

02-10-2026 11:42:26

За даними Nebius, постачальник хмарної інфраструктури підвищив тарифи на оренду GPU NVIDIA за запитом. Нові тарифи набувають чинності 1 жовтня 2026 року: вартість H100 зросла до 4,50 долара за GPU-годину з 3,85 долара (+16,9%), H200 — до 5,40 долара з 4,50 долара (+20%), B200 — до 8,50 долара з 7,15 долара (+18,9%), а B300 — до 9,50 долара з 7,85 долара (+21%). Зміни цін свідчать про стійкий дефіцит чипів на вторинному ринку. CoreWeave окремо оголосила 17 вересня, що продовжує укладати короткострокові контракти на обчислювальні потужності за вищими цінами: такі угоди укладаються за ціною, що відповідає приблизно 40 мільйонам доларів річного доходу з мегавата.

Nvidia rental prices are rising even for last-generation H100s. Nebius has posted an October 1, 2026 on-demand card that lifts selected Nvidia GPU-hour rates by 16.9% to 21.0%. CoreWeave said on September 17 that it is still signing compute at higher prices, including short contracts at about $40 million per megawatt of annualized revenue.
